en: Worship within your heart the dancer in the sky of supreme consciousness—the one whose state is both transcendent and immanent, who resounds with the jingling of his moving, beautiful anklets; who is the collyrium for the eyes of Patañjali, yet remains unstained and unwavering; who shatters the cycle of birth, possesses the luster of the kadamba flower and the garment of the sky, and has a throat like a cluster of dark clouds; he who is the jewel in the ocean of consciousness, the sun to the lotus-heart of the wise, and the cosmic actor upon the stage of the universal ether. 1.

Worship within your heart this ancient Supreme Consciousness, the Destroyer who shattered Tripura, whose bracelets are fashioned from the serpent Ananta, who is possessed of unbroken compassion and is free from internal defects; whose feet are meditated upon by Brahmā, the host of gods, and Indra; who wears the crescent moon as a crown; who has surpassed Yama through his supreme state; whose body is adorned with ashes; who is intent on deceiving Madana; who is the treasury accumulated for those who bow to him; and who is the sky of supreme consciousness. 2.

Worship in your heart Śiva, the Lord of Creatures (Paśupati), the Destroyer (Hara), who is the beginning of the entire world, whose virtues are unbreakable and lofty, who wears matted locks eager to support the mass of waves from the celestial river while holding the moon, who removes the pomp of Yama and destroys worldly existence; who extends his hand through the ten directions, holds a young deer in his palm, possesses eyes like the moon, fire, and the sun, and is the dancer in the sky of supreme consciousness.

[3] He is the stage for the rhythmic dancing of the gods Mukunda and Vidhi, resounding with the *jhala-jhala* and *jhala* sounds of his bracelets and tinkling bells set with infinite jewels, and echoing with the deep, resonant beat of the *maddala* drum held in their hands.

Worship in your heart the dancer in the sky of supreme consciousness, whose feet are saluted by Nanda, Sanaka, and other sages, who dwells in close proximity with Śakuntaratha, Barhiratha, Nandimukha, Dantimukha, and Bhṛṅgiriṭi;

who possesses infinite splendor, whose feet are worshipped by the gods, who resides within the hearts of sages, who is stainless, who is the wind carrying fragrance through the forest of the sky, who is the fire of the sacrifice, who is as beautiful as the sun, and who has a charming form. 4.

Worship in your heart the one of infinite glory, the jewel within the three worlds, the three-eyed one intent on the destruction of Tripura; him whose feet are saluted by joyful sages, who is full of compassion, the dancer in the sky of supreme consciousness. Worship in your heart the dancer in the sky of supreme consciousness—Paśupati, praised by Dhanañjaya, intent on pleasing those who bow before him, the destroyer of the elephant [of ignorance], a treasure-house of auspiciousness for the virtuous, who shows mercy to Rati; he whose neck is beautiful with the luster of an inconceivable swarm of bees, white as a cluster of blooming jasmine, wearing shimmering earrings of serpents that were worshipped by Mukunda and the hosts of gods.

Worship in your heart that Supreme Lord, the best of gods, the destroyer of the cities, Paśupati, who has generated the faces of the six [deities] beginning with Gajānana; Mṛḍa, whose matted locks are tawny like gold, who is the sun within the lotus of Sanaka, the wise one, the moonlight itself; the unattached-minded one who swallows the poison born from the ocean; the incomparable treasure-house of virtues, the granter of boons to Sananda; he of the tranquil moon-like face, the cosmic dancer in the sky of supreme consciousness. [And worship him] as the unborn, the chariot of the earth, whose string is the foremost of serpents, holding the golden-peaked bow, the deer shining in his hand, the broad axe, the supreme luster, the glow of saffron, and the hand-drum (ḍamaruka).

Worship in your heart this incomparable Mukunda, whose arrows grant fruitful results to those who bow before him, who is the steed for the multitude of the Vedas, who is fierce, who instantly destroyed the cities [of the demons], and who is the dancer in the sky of supreme consciousness. 8 Worship in your heart the son of Patañjali, the dancer in the sky of supreme consciousness, the enemy of the bodiless one (Kāma), the unborn, the bearer of the earth’s burden, the one who adorns all, who bears a blazing fire, the foe of Death (Antaka), whose feet are eternally worshipped by Indra and the gods, whose fragrant body possesses the luster of a mass of rays from hundreds of rising lotuses, and who is a parrot within the cage of the *praṇava*. 9

He who daily recites this hymn composed by the preeminent serpent, which always grants the vision of the two feet of the Lord— those beautiful feet devoid of hair and nails, born from the lake, praised by the divine beings headed by Indra and Viṣṇu, and which are the state of Śaṅkara— he goes to that supreme abode and never again to the ocean of birth, which produces supreme misery and bestows misfortune.
Thus ends the *Tāṇḍavāṣṭaka* composed by the venerable Patañjali. 10.
